MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the
hearing impaired, American Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and/or large print agendas. Please
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

AUDIO/VIDEO ACCESS TO BROADCASTED MEETINGS: City Council and Planning Commission meetings are televised live
on HBTV-3 Channel 3, and can be viewed via live or archived website at https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com.

7.. Update of the City COVID-19 Response Plan and Actions for Review and Discussion  -  Action: agenda title only {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Oliver Chi presented a PowerPoint entitled ... COVID-19 Update, Situational Update (US Totals, Orange County, Huntington Beach, HB EMS Response Statistics), Local Available Hospital Resources, California Containment Strategy Modeling, and Questions. \par
\par
Police Chief Robert Handy provided an overview of the May 1 active protest in the downtown area. Public education up front, unable to manage social distancing for everyone ... fine line for what can and cannot be enforced.  City team did a great job, PD, PW, mutual aid, mounted unit ... several pop up protests over the weekend ... small in size ... Main Street problems with opened businesses ... challenges with crowd, adjusted deployments, addressing issues with business owners.  Frustrations/shifting enforcement posture ... 20 officers needed to control Main Street.\par
\par
Closed the beach as a city - uncooperative visitors on the beach ... hundreds on the beach pre-dawn; beach clear by 10:00 am - beach path problems, where are the lines to be drawn?  Will continue to enforce Council decisions - Police are in a difficult position ... \par
\par
 \par
\par
Councilmember Hardy expressed frustration with being criticized for actions when we exist between two state (open) beaches.  She asked if staff has been able to work together with state officials to develop a plan.   Chi confirmed ... staff's actions with varied agencies in process ...\par
\par
Hardy asked if the state was aware of the planned protest?  Chi said yes ... multiple sites with similar protests ... Los Angeles, Ventura, San Diego ... Chief Handy did meet with organizers ... hopes of peaceful protest ... other groups tagging onto the event ...  \par
\par
Hardy thanked all involved in managing the May day event.\par
 \par
\par
Councilmember Posey discussed the relative low number of people at the protest.\par
\par
Councilmember Hardy asked for the price on filing a lawsuit ... Attorney Gates said the lawsuit will not cost the taxpayers any money.\par
\par
Councilmember Carr challenged Attorney Gates comment suggesting that the lawsuit against the state is being paid for by other agencies.\par
\par
Posey questioned costs associated with staff costs to move the lawsuit forward.\par
}


CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopted (Pass)

13.. Adopt Resolution No. 2020-29 to authorize and adopt a Five-Year Plan for Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program Funds and to submit an application for funding in year 1 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021)  -  Action: approved (Pass) {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Travis Hopkins, Assistant City Manager, provided a PP entitled Public Hearing:  Permanent Local Housing Allocation, that included the following titled slides:  PLHA Funds (2), Proposed PLHA 5-Year Plan (2), PLHA Application, and City Council Options. \par
\par
Peterson questioned the annual costs to run the shelter... Hopkins said details being worked out ... approximately $1.5M ... Chi and Hopkins discussed further recommendations will be heard at a later date (CDBG ...)\par
\par
Delgleize questioned if the County contribution will be recognized ... chi described details.\par
\par
Peterson questioned County timeline ... 10 week assumption ... is the County finishing no matter what??  Chi ensured the project would be finished.\par
\par
Councilmember Posey questioned if the housing element certification help us land these funds?  Chi agreed.  Housing element would need to be approved to receive the funds.\par
}


ADMINISTRATIVE ITEMS

14.. Recommendations for establishing the Huntington Beach Economic Recovery Task Force  -  Action: approved (Pass) {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Councilmember Posey requested that the Mayor define what success will look like for economic recovery efforts.  Mayor Semeta discussed how the task force will focus specifically on COVID-19.  Discussion ensued on the business plan - Posey wants a business plan defined - Semeta says the task force will create a business plan - Posey would like the plan brought back before the Council - \par
\par
Councilmember Delgleize - how do we determine who the list represents ... restrictions on serving on multiple commissions/committees ... Semeta suggests the process follow past practice in selecting participants ... can return with recommendations ... local involvement ... 2.b framework - two council assigned ... Semeta stated Chi has been in touch with interested parties ... \par
\par
Carr suggested a health expert be included in this committee ... child care as well ... time is of the essence ... meet more than once a month\par
\par
Peterson discussed possible appointments ... very qualified parties in mind ... group will determine success ... initial business plan does come from task force ... \par
\par
Councilmember Brenden supports the concept ... slightly concerned about agility and nimbleness from a task force - great staff involvement needed; concerned about the task force will be paralyzed in scope - needs a plan in place prior; large businesses drowning out small businesses ... wants a scope identified in two weeks - success criteria, etc., ... governance isn't always the answer to problem ... let's get our small businesses back to work - we're at a critical point of forming the task force ... need identified goals/objectives etc.\par
\par
Mayor Semeta expressed the importance of a plan to assist our businesses ... Mr. Chi ... can staff be incorporated into a larger number of meetings?  Yes ... more at first to get the plan off the ground.  strategic objectives identified early.\par
\par
Councilmember Carr - Health expert so important for guidance ... safe and healthy process ...\par
\par
Peterson - County representative for health ???\par
}


15.. Adopt Resolution No. 2020-30 supporting the Orange County Board of Supervisors’ efforts to address Commercial Re-Openings in response to COVID-19  -  Action: approved (Pass)
